key_insight: Quenched B-site disorder in monoclinic Sr2FeRuO6 stabilizes a Griffiths-like magnetic regime with short-range ferromagnetic clusters and strongly localized charge transport.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how controlled cation disorder in 3d-4d double perovskites can tune magnetic inhomogeneity and hopping-based transport for spintronic materials design.
method: Structural characterization of the monoclinic, antisite-disordered double perovskite.
Magnetic measurements to identify a robust Griffiths phase above the ordering temperature.
Electrical transport analysis to distinguish small-polaron hopping and variable-range hopping behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports magnetic and transport data showing a Griffiths phase above the transition temperature and a temperature-dependent crossover from small-polaron hopping to variable-range hopping.
watch_item: Because the behavior is strongly tied to disorder and localization, performance may be sensitive to synthesis quality and antisite concentration.
paper_title: Disorder-Induced Griffiths like Phase and Charge Localization in Sr2FeRuO6
